entries.name: The Massive Entertainment block
entries.summary: Several factories and workplaces were established along the lively Bergsgatan in late 19th century, specialising in textiles, cars, chocolate, bread, and much more.
entries.description: Several factories and workplaces were established along the lively Bergsgatan in late 19th century, specialising in textiles, cars, chocolate, bread, and much more. The city grew rapidly during this period, with the population approximately doubling every twenty years. Many of the new residents of Möllevångarna made their living here. The red brick buildings were the home of Fabriks AB Scandinavia, which manufactured ribbons, yarn, thread and buttons, as well as having a woodwork division. A Danish-owned company, it employed 250 to 300 people here in its heyday. During the First World War, there were restrictions on imports so the factory mostly produced yarn made from paper. Nowadays, the games company Massive is based here. Photographs: Malmö City Archive, Malmö City History

entries.name: Henrik Menander 1853-1917
entries.summary: Har man någon gång hört Arbetets söner, vars text Henrik Menander skrev, eller den svenska versionen av Internationalen, som han översatte, då har man stiftat hans bekantskap.
entries.description: Har man någon gång hört Arbetets söner, vars text Henrik Menander skrev, eller den svenska versionen av Internationalen, som han översatte, då har man stiftat hans bekantskap. Uppväxt som dräng på landsbygden utbildade han sig till korkskärare och vandrade som gesäll i stora delar av Europa. Vid återkomsten till Sverige engagerade han sig i den unga socialistiska rörelsen och arbetade en tid nära August Palm. Att han var fackligt och politiskt engagerad ledde till svartlistning och under en period hade Henrik väldigt svårt att få arbete. Väl i Malmö arbetade han regelbundet för tidningen Arbetet.

entries.name: Bertil 1851-1918 & Anna Sederholm 1868-1933
entries.summary: Bertil och Anna Sederholms gravplats är ett Parthenon i mindre skala.
entries.description: Bertil och Anna Sederholms gravplats är ett Parthenon i mindre skala. Herren är min herde, från en bön ur psaltaren, står det under det imposanta korset. Konsuln och grosshandlaren Bertil Sederholm var även portugisisk vicekonsul och österrike-ungersk konsul samt ledamot av stadsfullmäktige i Malmö. Familjen bodde i pampiga villa Saaris vid Lundavägen, ett mindre slott med en park omkring. Hustrun Anna var filantrop och engagerade sig i insamlingen av pengar till byggandet av Kirsebergskyrkan.

entries.description: ända sedan parken grundades har det funnits växthus på området där plantor drivits upp och grönsaker odlats. Längan längs med Norra Parkgatan byggdes redan på 1920-talet och utökades 1943. Fyrtio år senare hade plantorna försvunnit och Terrariet, Malmö Reptilcenter invigdes. Här har sedan dess besökare kunnat studera tropiska djur - ormar, spindlar, apor och krokodiler för att bara nämna några. Under tio år på 2000-talet bodde även papegojan Douglas på Terrariet, han var född 1967 och spelade med i Pippi Långstrump-filmerna, då som kapten Efraim Långstrumps goja. Här utvann oljeslageriet olja ur lin, raps och solrosfrön för bruk inom målning och industri. Såpfabriken hade en mycket omfattande tillverkning - såpa, soda, tvål, glycerin, vattenglas och kosmetiska artiklar var de största tillverkningsgrenarna. entries.summary: Pehr Fricks fabriker låg här ca 1911 - 1929 och bedrev cichoria och tobaksfabriksrörelse samt förarbete av trävaror .
entries.description: Pehr Fricks fabriker låg här ca 1911 - 1929 och bedrev cichoria och tobaksfabriksrörelse samt förarbete av trävaror . Från och med 1916 fram till nedläggningen sommaren 1929 levererade fabriken, som var den enda i sitt slag i landet, cigarrlådor till tobaksmonopolet. Tillverkningen upphörde dels på grund av minskad cigarrkonsumtion och dels för att man övergick till att förpacka i pappaskar. Cigarrlådorna tillverkades huvudsakligen av cederträ. Vanligen finnas också badrum, där vart och ett av barnen får sitt bad var eller varannan vecka. Detta bad jämte en god hygien i skolrummen beträffande vädring och städning gör, att vi inte känna mycket av den förskämda luft, som fanns i folkskolans rum i gamla tider. I somliga skolhus finnas till och med rum, där barnen bibringas den nyttiga vanan att borta tänder.

entries.name: Lilla Venedig
entries.summary: At the start of the 19th century, the private estate known as Sofielundsgården was split into plots and sold off to two groups of people moving in different dir
entries.description: At the start of the 19th century, the private estate known as Sofielundsgården was split into plots and sold off to two groups of people moving in different directions: workers escaping the over-crowded city, and poor rural folk being drawn towards it. By the late 1870s, this area (now known as Sofielund) had grown to become a solidly working-class district, south of the city limits. In 1896, it became a municipality society, a semi-independent administrative unit. By 1900, the Kammarkolligiet an influential department in the Ministry of Finance was pushing for Sofielund to be incorporated into the city of Malmö. This was resisted by the Kunglig Majestät the administrative organ of the Swedish monarchy which argued that it shouldn t be part of Malmö because it lacked "sewers, school buildings, fire extinguishing tools and paving on the streets". Idunsgatan was originally called Storgatan, but changed its name when Sofielund was finally incorporated in 1911. Sofielund was called Little Venice because of its tendency to flood. In 1917, 1920 and 1924, it ended up looking like this photograph.

De åldras och precis som människor har de många berättelser att berätta för den som är beredd att titta och lyssna. Du kanske har sett den här byggnaden många gånger förr. Men vad hände här för hundra år sedan? Kanske kan foto-kollaget de satt upp på fasaden ge någon ledtråd? Men oj, där föll något! En glasskärva. Eller är det kanske ett fönster in i det förgångna? entries.name: Trikåfabriken - Den ståtliga bilen
entries.summary: Scania bilfabrik är Sveriges första bilfabrik.
entries.description: Scania bilfabrik är Sveriges första bilfabrik. Härifrån rullar det ena underverket efter det andra ut på gatorna och vidare upp i landet. Trots att de har hållit på ett par år nu är varje ny modell fortfarande en fröjd att se. Mekaniker: "Vilken skönhet!" Erik: "Jepp! Den har jag varit med och gjort fjädringen på! Och vet du vad? I morgon ska jag ta ut den på en tur med Trine. Då får vi se hur bra fjädringen är på riktigt." Mekaniker: "I morgon? Jobbar du inte i morgon?" Erik: "Nä, Sven är skyldig mig en tjänst och Trine verkar alltid komma undan med vad som helst." Mekaniker: "Trine? Jag trodde att du var tillsammans med hon den andra vadheterhon Magdalena?" Erik: "Vad kan jag säga. Jag är populär!" Mekaniker: "Du är fanemig helt oförbättrelig!"

entries.description: Finns det några som ser allt i kvarteret är dekorationshuvudena på fasaden längs Monbijougatan. De har dessutom inget bättre för sig än att skvallra om det. Huvud 1: "Se hur alla rusar förbi. Det känns som om alla har bråttom nu för tiden." Huvud 2: "Eller hur? Annat var det på vår tid!" Huvud 1: "Precis. Men du, påminn mig igen: när var vår tid?" Huvud 2: "Jag såg en flicka komma rusande förbi, precis efter att det hände. Hon grät så att det skvalade." Huvud 1: "Jag såg henne också. Hon stannade och lutade sig mot soptunnan där borta. Helt förstörd, stackarn Jag tittade bort för jag tänkte att hon kanske kräktes." Huvud 2: "Ja, uschiane mig! Fast kjolen on hade på sig var inte så klädsam." Huvud 1: "Nej, modet nu för tiden förstår jag inte på mig alls..."

entries.summary: Jon: "Tack för att ni berättar om allt ni sett och lärt er.
entries.description: Jon: "Tack för att ni berättar om allt ni sett och lärt er. Vi visste att vi kunde lite på er!" Alma: "En del av det ni berättar är jobbigt att höra för oss båda men saker börjar klarna nu. Det känns som om vi behöver en eller två detaljer till för att jag ska få de svar jag behöver." Jon: "Ni har varit så fina och jag vill inte stressa er men både jag och Alma känner att något håller på att förändras. Som om krafter som hållit oss kvar här så länge är på upphällningen. Vad ni än gör nu så är det bråttom." Alma: "Vi är både så tacksamma för att ni tar er tid. Men om ni vill hjälpa oss att gräva vidare tror jag att ni måste välja vilken ledtråd ni vill följa vidare. Jag tror inte ni kommer att ha tid att hjälpa oss båda." Jon: "Om det är som du säger Alma och du brukar ha rätt då finns det bara ett val. Jag insisterar på att ni ska hjälpa Alma. Jag accepterar inget annat." Vid nästa kartplupp måste du välja - Vill du gräva vidare i Almas eller Jons historia?

entries.summary: Suellska villan. Fin som snus när den en gång byggdes i slutet på sjuttonhundratalet - men i sämre skick nu på 1920-talet.
entries.description: Suellska villan. Fin som snus när den en gång byggdes i slutet på sjuttonhundratalet - men i sämre skick nu på 1920-talet. Enligt rykten i området har en del ljusskygga individer flyttat in. Bland de unga kvinnorna som hamnat i olycka och blivit med barn mot sin vilja viskas det om att det bor en änglamakerska på vinden. Vad en änglamakerska är? Det är ett av de där yrkena man bäst talar tyst om för det är så hemskt att hjärtat fladdrar när man tänker på det. Men vi kan säga så här: om du på denna tid födde ett barn som du inte ville eller kunde ta hand om mer så kunde du ge det till änglamakerskan så behövde du aldrig tänka på det barnet mer Hu!

Men här kommer något annat. Fint folk, minsann! Direktör Rodengren: "Fin dag, Siersen, fin dag!" Siersen: "I sanning, broder!" Direktör Rodengren: "Du, hur har det gått med jakten på en ny maskintekniker?" Siersen: "Bra, bra. Andersson kom förbi och ansökte om jobbet. Han, chefsmekanikern på Scania bilfabrik. Han ska ju vara otroligt händig mekaniskt har jag hört." Direktör Rodengren: "Honom skulle jag vara försiktig men om jag var du." Siersen:" Hurså?" Direktör Rodengren: "Ja, det pratas en del. Han har en del problem med du vet Direktör Rodengren gör en drickande rörelse med armen samtidigt som han gör kluck-ljud Siersen: "Säg inget mer, broder."

entries.description: Den nybyggda Betesdakyrkan i närheten av trikåfabriken håller i minnesgudstjänsten för Alma. En liten samling sörjande samlas för att minnas och för att trösta varandra. På avstånd tittar medarbetare från trikåfabriken på, ovilliga att störa i familjens sorg men samtidigt för nyfikna för att kunna hålla sig borta. Trikåflicka 1: "Det där måste vara Almas föräldrar. Stackarna!" Trikåflicka 2: "Ja, hur de ska klara sig nu! Alma skickade pengar varje vecka, hörde jag. Det var därför hon aldrig var med och dansade på Moriskan." Trikåflicka 1: "Jag ser att Trine inte är här. Lite dålig stil, tycker jag. Lika som bär och tillsammans jämnt. Man tycker ju att hon åtminstone kunde dyka upp till minnesstunden." Trikåflicka 2: "Ja, jag har inte sett henne sen det hände." Trikåficka 1: "Allting är så konstigt. Varför var Alma ens på trikåfabriken den dagen, hon var ju ledig " Vi lämnar där dem. entries.description: Moriska paviljongen, eller Moriskan som alla säger, är ett nöjespalats i Folket park. Här kan man både äta och dans och på helgerna är det livat. Ibland lite för livat. Trine: "Håll dig borta från honom om du vet vad som är bra för dig!" Matilda: "Ha! Du bara inbillar dig om du tror att Erik är intresserad av en sådan som dig!" Trine: "Det kom ju från rätt käft! Dygdiga lilla fröken skit-trist! Erik tycker bara synd om dig. Det är därför han inte bett dig fara och flyga än." Matilda: "Säg det där igen, Trine så ska jag se till att ge dig en sådan tjottablängare att inte ens du kommer ha smink nog att täcka över det." Trine: "Hotar du mig? Jaja. Ska det vara så kan jag också. Antingen slutar du träffa Erik eller så berättar jag för fabrikör Holmberg om vad som hände med din bäbis, Matilda. Ja, se inte så förvånad ut. Jag vet nog att du gav bort han till änglamakerskan på Sulleska villan!" Matilda: "Lögnare! Du skulle aldrig våga!" Trine: "Vi får väl se!"

entries.description: Det gäller att värdera allt bra i livet för på ett ögonblick kan det vara borta. Flickan faller från trikåfabrikens tredje våning. Hinner hon ens förstå vad som händer? Strax innan har hon stått vid fönstret och undersökt mönstret på en provbit och nu är döden bara meter bort. Allt hon drömt om har tagits ifrån henne av någon som hon inte ens vet vem det är. entries.name: Rosenvingehuset
entries.summary: "Ack människa, betänk din lott Hur Gud av jord dig skapat blott Hur döden smyger, tjuven lik Och rycker bort både arm och rik." Så lyder inskriptionen i den bil
entries.description: "Ack människa, betänk din lott Hur Gud av jord dig skapat blott Hur döden smyger, tjuven lik Och rycker bort både arm och rik." Så lyder inskriptionen i den bildsten du ser ovanför ingången till huset. Den som lät bygga detta hus var Anna Pedersdatter Lilliefeldt som 1534 flyttade in i huset. Hennes man Mogens Jensen Rosenvinge, handsekreterare åt kung Kristian II, var död redan innan huset byggdes men han har ändå gett namn åt det. Anne var moster till Citze Kortzdatter van Nuland, gift med Jörgen Kock paret bodde snett över gatan - och var ursprungligen från Helsingör där hennes far var borgmästare. Huset byggdes som ett parhus, ett hus med två spegelvända lägenheter. Utanför huset fanns försäljningsbodar med diskar och luckor ut mot nuvarande Västergatan. I huset fann man vid restaurering Nordens äldsta papperstapet. Bild: Mogen Jensen Rosenvinges vapensköld samt bilder ur boken Bager: Rosenvingeska huset, 1969.

entries.name: Matilda Olsson 1849-1920
entries.summary: Matilda Olsson och Anders Påhlsson gifte sig 1874.
entries.description: Matilda Olsson och Anders Påhlsson gifte sig 1874. Samma höst flyttade de till Malmö. Matilda bakade bröd i sitt hem och maken som var snickare på Kockums hade börjat ta upp beställningar av sina arbetskamrater och levererat brödet till dem på arbetet. Detta togs inte väl emot på arbetsplatsen, Anders blev ombedd att sluta sälja bröd eller lämna sitt arbete. Han valde brödet och med hjälp av Matildas arv kunde paret så 1878 starta sitt företag, A. Påhlssons bageri som fortfarande är ett familjeföretag. Bageriet expanderade och ett flertal butiker startades. 1965 ändras företagsnamnet till Pågens familjebageri AB och senare har det förkortats till Pågen. För några år sedan lanserade Pågen ett nytt bröd med gamla anor, ett surdegsbröd som kallas Matildas efter grundaren av företaget. Man hittade en handskriven receptbok från 1892 och använde sig att dessa recept när man lanserade nya bröd.

entries.name: Otto Ohm 1860-1920
entries.summary: På stenen finns förutom namnen en Kristussymbol; den första och den sista bokstaven i det grekiska alfabetet, alfa och .
entries.description: På stenen finns förutom namnen en Kristussymbol; den första och den sista bokstaven i det grekiska alfabetet, alfa och . Många ur familjen Ohm har varit fotografer, det här är en av pionjärerna. Otto d.ä. var son till fotografen Heinrich som senare bodde i Köpenhamn. Familjen flyttade vidare till Skåne innan Otto, efter att ha blivit upplärd av den legendariske fotografen Carl de Sh rengrad (som för övrigt också vilar på S:t Pauli norra kyrkogård), öppnade egen rörelse på Rundelsgatan i Malmö. Tillsammans med hustrun Amelie fick Otto nio barn, äldste sonen döptes också han till Otto. För att inte sammanblanda de båda kallades sonen för Bebbe.

entries.name: Kristianstadsgatan 16
entries.summary: This building, designed by architect Hans Thyselius, was once home to Centralmejeriet (the Central Dairy).
entries.description: This building, designed by architect Hans Thyselius, was once home to Centralmejeriet (the Central Dairy). The business was founded in 1907 and was originally located on Amiralsgatan 8. Once the company expanded, they needed their own premises, which they found here on Kristianstadsgatan in 1923. The company sold and distributed dairy products through their own stores throughout Malmö. In more recent times, this location has housed a cinema and Caf Glassfabriken. Photograph: Malmö stadsarkiv, Orkester-Journalen

entries.name: Oscar Hjalmar Wiens 1846-1923
entries.summary: Oscar Hjalmar kallades O.H och etablerade sig i Malmö 1874.
entries.description: Oscar Hjalmar kallades O.H och etablerade sig i Malmö 1874. Med sin bror Fingal och entreprenören Bertil Sederholm sålde han vin och sprit till näringsställen. För att garantera avsättningen köpte man flera gästgiverier i Skåne. O.H var dessutom skeppsredare vilket lönade sig bra under första världskriget. Det Wienska palatset i korsningen östergatan/Prostgatan är ett av Malmös pampigaste bostadshus från slutet av 1800-talet. Huset ritades av den välkände arkitekten Alfred Arwidius. I bottenplanet fanns en butik där varorna såldes, under fastigheten en stor källare där dryckerna buteljerades. Oscar Wiens och hans familj bodde i fastigheten men flyttade 1917 till Löberöds gård.

entries.name: Barnekows Laboratorium
entries.summary: Barnekows laboratorium grundades i Malmö år 1878 av den danske ingenjören Sophus von Barnekow och blev Sveriges första fabrik för mejeripreparat.
entries.description: Barnekows laboratorium grundades i Malmö år 1878 av den danske ingenjören Sophus von Barnekow och blev Sveriges första fabrik för mejeripreparat. Bolaget var kännt för sina förstklassiga tillverkningar av mejeripreparat och försäljer därjämte alla till mejeribranschen hörande utensilier så som ostlöpe, smörfärg, ostfärg och syreväckare . Företaget utmärkte sig även genom att redan 1923 ha en kvinnlig verkställande direktör, fröken Ester Hallberg, och på trettiotalet var inte mindre än tre av de fem personerna i bolagets styrelse kvinnor.

entries.name: Södervärns vattentorn
entries.summary: Södervärn's water tower was designed by city architect Salomon Sörensen.
entries.description: Södervärn's water tower was designed by city architect Salomon Sörensen. 54 metres high, it was inaugurated in 1916 and replaced both the Kirseberg water tower and Pildammstornet. When it was completed, Sofielund could finally be connected to the municipal water network. The tower stayed in use until 2015. In the first photograph, you can see a splash pond in front of the tower. Known locally as Söderhavet (the Southern Sea), it was a magnet for young people in the summer take the tram to Sofielund! Looking at the tower today, you can still see a a brighter section on one side, just under its copper roof. It stems from an incident in April 1983, while the roof was being repaired. A man climbed up the scaffolding with a can of paint and a brush. He then painted, "MURDER CARS HATE DATA" on the side of the tower (it doesn t really make much sense in Swedish either). The text had to be blasted away, and the impact is still, just about, visible today.

entries.name: Norregatan/Stora Kvarngatan
entries.summary: Här syns hur den äldre bebyggelsen fullständigt rivits för att ge plats åt opåkallat mycket postmodernism, inte minst i kvarteret Storken.
entries.description: Här syns hur den äldre bebyggelsen fullständigt rivits för att ge plats åt opåkallat mycket postmodernism, inte minst i kvarteret Storken. På väggen i den gamla bilden hänger affischer som gör reklam för Folkets Park, tidningen Arbetet och en stor idrottsfest med dragkamp som ska hållas å Idrottsplatsen. Det bärande namnet i Folkets Park-annonsen är Harry Persson, skådespelaren och sångaren som via hustrun Stina gifte in sig i underhållningsfamiljen Hellqvist. (Svärfar Anders var tidvis teaterdirektör och kuplettsångare och dennes syster Olga känd komedienne). Vi vet att Harry scendebuterade 1928 och kan således datera bilden någorlunda. Foto: Jeanette Rosengrens samling

entries.name: Hans Krondahl
entries.summary: Malmö s principal art gallery, Malmö Konsthall, houses a large Hans Krondahl (1929 2018) collection.
entries.description: Malmö s principal art gallery, Malmö Konsthall, houses a large Hans Krondahl (1929 2018) collection. He was one of Sweden's foremost textile artists. In 1955 he was accepted to a textile degree course at Stockholm s University of Arts, Crafts and Design (Konstfack). In the early 1970s, he collaborated with the internationally renowned designer Katja af Sweden and Malmö Mekaniska Trikåfabrik. Throughout his career he designed fabrics for numerous collections with patterns that shaped contemporary expressive fashion. Krondahl was openly gay. Foto: Malmö Stadsarkiv Text: A Ride to Pride en kartguide till Malmös hbtqi-historia, Malmö Stadsarkiv

entries.name: Omnibusstationen
entries.summary: In 1887, horse-drawn trams were introduced to Malmö, operated by a private company.
entries.description: In 1887, horse-drawn trams were introduced to Malmö, operated by a private company. 10 years later two omnibus companies popped up, providing horse-drawn carriages for the masses. It wasn t until 1905 that the city took control of public transport, and then electrified the tram network a year later. Municipal bus lines ran alongside more expensive private competitors from 1929. Number 16 was the first motorized bus line in Malmö. The number 15 buses that you can see in the picture, travelled from the central omnibus station to Kulladal. Fricksgatan is on the right. It's part of the Abel neighborhood, which has been completely transformed since the photograph was taken. Foto: Jeanette Rosengrens samling

entries.name: Sofielunds industriområde
entries.summary: At the start of the 20th century, most of Malmö s factories were still located in the city centre.
entries.description: At the start of the 20th century, most of Malmö s factories were still located in the city centre. City planners encouraged the flight to dedicated industrial areas in the decades that followed, and Norra Grängesbergsgatan became an important street from the early 1930s. Industry around this area expanded in line with the city s wishes, boosted by easy access to the Continental railway line (it links Malmö to the port at Trelleborg, and thus to Europe). A lot of the streets in this area are named after Swedish manufacturers. The picture shows the old electricity substation in the foreground. Photograph: Malmö stadsarkiv
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Jesusparken
entries.summary: Falsterboplan is almost universally known as Jesusparken.
entries.description: Falsterboplan is almost universally known as Jesusparken. The name comes from the fact that Malmö s church congregations owned this land and planned to build a church here. However, a change of plan in 1928 meant that Västra Skrävlinge church hall which is now known as St. Mary's Church was rebuilt instead. This patch of land became an allotment site as a result. The picture shows the small colony cottages in the 1930s. Just a few decades earlier, during and immediately after the First World War, these cottages (and hundreds of others in Möllevången and Sofielund) provided housing for Malmö residents in desperate times.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Pågen & Gustav Möller
entries.summary: The section of Möllevångsgatan, west of Södra Förstadsgatan, was previously called Tallgatan.
entries.description: The section of Möllevångsgatan, west of Södra Förstadsgatan, was previously called Tallgatan. In these modest two-storey houses in 1878, Matilda Olsson and her husband Anders Påhlsson started their bakery Påhlsson's Bread . Today it s know as Pågen). Their sourdough bread, from Matild as own receipe, was a particular success, and the company soon grew. For a long time, the bread was sold straight from their oven, before they eventually moved into a factory in a new building at 12 Bergsgatan. The building on Möllevångsgatan was also the Gustav Möller s childhood home. He would go on to become Minister of Social Affairs in Per Albin Hansson's government. During his tenure, social reforms like child allowance, universal dental care and the national pension were introduced. Photographs: Jeanette Rosengren s collection, Pågen, Wikipedia
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Sofielundsgården
entries.summary: Here you can see the south facade of Sofielundsgården's main building.
entries.description: Here you can see the south facade of Sofielundsgården's main building. The land reform of 1786 (the first of many in Skåne, through to the 19th century), saw the villages here essentially demolished. They were replaced with individual, contiguous plots with a cottage in the middle each family would now farm their own land rather than contributing to the old, more communal type of agriculture. Governor Tage Thott was assigned property in the far west of this area, in what was then called ängavången. Here, Thott worked 150 acres of farmland. In 1792, it was bought by the merchant Hans Bauert and renamed Sofielund, after his wife Sophia Charlotta af Trolle. Several buildings were erected on the farm, and a six-acre park was created. b Hans Bauert died in 1802 and Sophia af Trolle in 1805. After that, merchant Per Jacobsson bought the land, selling it on in 1823. In the summer of 1837, the renowned bishop and future academy member Johan Henrik Thomander hired Sofielund, and often gathered his friends together here for food and drink in the rural environment. Ownership continued to regularly change hands, until the city of Malmö became purchased it. The main building was demolished in 1953, although some details were saved and sent to a museum: two round earthenware-tiled stoves, wood panelling, a stair railing, doors, fittings, and the fire insurance certificate! This picture was taken around 1930.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Lönngården
entries.summary: In the early 1930s, the Lönngården area was established.
entries.description: In the early 1930s, the Lönngården area was established. It comprised thirteen similar buildings, all with slanted roofs and sides facing on to Lönngatan. They were designed by Carl-Axel Stoltz, who would go on to become Malmö s city architect. The buildings had four apartments on each of their four floors, with six staircases. They were extraordinarily modern at the time of construction, and they all had a bathroom, laundry room, pantry and storage space in the basement. The apartments were quite small though. On the right of the picture you can see the part of the Malmö-Ystad railway. When this was closed down in the early 1970s, a cycle path was put in its place. Photograph: Jeanette Rosengrens samling
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Majken Johansson (1930-1993)
entries.summary: Majken Johansson was one of Sweden's most notable poets of the second half of the 20th century.
entries.description: Majken Johansson was one of Sweden's most notable poets of the second half of the 20th century. She was born out of wedlock to a young waitress in Malmö, then lived with a foster family at this address until she was 13. In 1952, her first collection of poems was published. It contained what would become her most well-remembered line of poetry: Mitt namn är Ma-ha-ha-jken Joha-honsson. She had a secret relationship with female director Solveig Borg, which ended with Borg s suicide. Borg appears in all Johansson s subsequent poetry collections, referred to only as "S". In 1958, Johansson joined the Salvation Army. One of her poems ends with a line that is especially characteristic of her work, a mixture of darkness, hope and playfulness: "Hallelujah ANYWAY!". Foto: Malmö Stadsarkiv Text adapted from: A Ride to Pride en kartguide till Malmös hbtqi-historia, Malmö Stadsarkiv
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Elisabethsystrarnas sjukhem
entries.summary: Den katolska kongregationen med samma namn består av kvinnor som vill hjälpa andra, oavsett religion eller samhällsklass.
entries.description: Den katolska kongregationen med samma namn består av kvinnor som vill hjälpa andra, oavsett religion eller samhällsklass. Verksamheten grundades i Tyskland 1842 och kom till Malmö 1874. Då hjälpte kvinnorna till i den katolska skolan och bedrev ambulerande sjukvård. På Lilla Nygatan 3 ligger fortfarande huset som mellan 1930 2007 inhyste det sjukhus som senare blev sjukhem. Huset rymde 22 bäddar och var när det uppfördes väldigt modernt. Fortfarande finns skulpturen över det ungerska helgonet S:ta Elisabeth i en nisch över porten, med krona och en korg med rosor står hon där dag och natt och vakar. Foto: Jeanette Rosengrens samling
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Max Engeström 1867-1930
entries.summary: Max Engeströms far Edvard var ägare av och en av grundarna till sockerfabriken i Arlöv, en post som togs över av Max efter faderns död.
entries.description: Max Engeströms far Edvard var ägare av och en av grundarna till sockerfabriken i Arlöv, en post som togs över av Max efter faderns död. Då hette företaget Svenska Sockerfabriks AB. Vid Limhamnsvägen lät Max, som också var belgisk konsul, tillsammans med hustrun Margarete anlägga Fridhemsborg som i folkmun kallas Engeströmska palatset. En villa omfattande 1200 kvadratmeter och 40 rum! I mitten av 1950-talet sålde familjen villan till skeppsredaren och förläggaren Einar Hansen.

entries.name: Bussgaraget
entries.summary: Bussgaraget byggdes 1932 och låg då i stadens utkant.
entries.description: Bussgaraget byggdes 1932 och låg då i stadens utkant. Det tidigare storkvarteret Spårvägen omgavs av Zenithgatan, Celsiusgatan, Industrigatan och Nobelvägen. Här har Malmö stad ägt all mark. Delar av Malmö Konsthögskola huserar nu i båghallarna sedan höstterminen 2018. På grund av oljebrist som uppstod under andra världskriget kördes många bussar med hjälp av gengasaggregat som sattes längst bak på fordonet. Den giftiga gasen ledde till många olyckor. Foto Stadsarkivet Christian Kindblads samlingar

entries.name: Christopher Isherwood at the Grand Hotel
entries.summary: Christopher Isherwood (1904-1986) was a gay British writer, best known for his book Farewell to Berlin, later filmed as Cabaret.
entries.description: Christopher Isherwood (1904-1986) was a gay British writer, best known for his book Farewell to Berlin, later filmed as Cabaret. On November 30, 1934, Isherwood paid a visit to Malmö. In his autobiography "Christopher and his Kind" he mentioned how well he was received. He came to Malmö to give a lecture titled, "My Experiences in an English Film Studio". Before the lecture, Isherwood was taken to the Grand Hotel, where apparently he was given quite a lot to drink. He was fairly inebriated by the time of his lecture, but he quickly noticed that the audience was also drunk. The lecture was a success! Photo 1: from a postcard in a private collection. Photo 2: By National Media Museum from UK - W. H. Auden and Christopher Isherwood en route to China, 1938. Text: Jeanette Rosengren, Kira förlag
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Malmö Östra Sjukhus (1935–1995)
entries.summary: Olga Börjesson was chief physician at Malmö s psychiatric hospital.
entries.description: Olga Börjesson was chief physician at Malmö s psychiatric hospital. In the early 1940s, 20 men were charged with "moral crimes" relating to homosexual acts, and two of them were, according to Börjesson, in need of mental health treatment. At the same time, a legislative proposal was being prepared, with the aim of decriminalizing homosexuality. The proposal committee noted that there was a lack of knowledge around female homosexuality, and so a group of experts, including Börjesson, were asked to answer a questionnaire. In her questionnaire, Böriesson described nurses and students who, when in love, had become either affectionate or jealous. She d noticed the latter emotion only in those in relationships with men. "For my part, I would think that female homosexuality is not a socially dangerous phenomenon in our country," she stated. Foto: Malmö Stadsarkiv Text: A Ride to Pride en kartguide till Malmös hbtqi-historia, Malmö Stadsarkiv
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Dama-Verken
entries.summary: The company was actually called AB Damm- och Spånledningar, but no-one around here would ever say that: Dama-Verken was the name that stuck.
entries.description: The company was actually called AB Damm- och Spånledningar, but no-one around here would ever say that: Dama-Verken was the name that stuck. They started in 1909, and moved to newly built premises on Lantmannagatan in 1936. The office building and the machine hall were on the same site, as well as an air-raid shelter where the staff would park their bikes. And what did they make? Well, fans and ventilation shafts mostly, as well as some other equipment associated with air conditioning and drying. They also made those classic metal lockers made from sheet metal that have graced innumerable workplaces over the years. Photograph: Malmö-boken, 1946
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Saturnus
entries.summary: Founded in 1893, AB Fabriken Saturnus moved to their newly built premises on Lantmannagatan in 1937.
entries.description: Founded in 1893, AB Fabriken Saturnus moved to their newly built premises on Lantmannagatan in 1937. Offices, factories and warehouses were all set up here in the new industrial district. Designed by architect Stig F Johansson, the new building cost 200,000 kronor to build. The business was acquired by the Liepe family in 1920. Soft drinks were their main concern, but they also produced essences and seasonings derived from fruits and spices (their mulled wine mix was a big seller). Changes to licensing laws in 1995 enabled them to start making their own alcoholic beverages. Piratens Besk ( The Pirate s Bitters ) is one of their best known products. In 2000, the family business moved to Fosieby, on the outskirts of Malmö. Photography: Malmö-boken, 1946
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: AB Textilkonst
entries.summary: You don t hear about shoelace makers so often these days.
entries.description: You don t hear about shoelace makers so often these days. However, when this company started trading, back in 1932, shoelaces were their bread and butter (though they also made ribbons and lace). The shoelace business was booming apparently, because they built new premises on Norbergsgatan seven years later, incorporating both an office and a factory. The company was owned by the Ehnimb family, who were somewhat forward-thinking. The new home they built provided a decent environment for their workers modern, light, airy, with well-equipped lunch rooms and changing facilities. Their products developed over time, and they became well known for their lampshades (as well as their shoelaces). Photography: Malmö-boken, 1946
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Malmö Stadsarkiv
entries.summary: The City Archive (Malmö Stadsarkiv) is situated in the former premises of Arbetet newspaper.
entries.description: The City Archive (Malmö Stadsarkiv) is situated in the former premises of Arbetet newspaper. The Social Democrat publication was located in this building from 1939. Nowadays, the archive holds documents and pictures about Malmö's history, people and places. The collection contain material that reflects society's views on homosexuality and bisexuality throughout the years. This material includes documents from authorities such as the police and law courts, but also from organisations like RFSL Malmö and Lesbisk Front. Foto: Malmö Stadsarkiv Text adapted from: A Ride to Pride en kartguide till Malmös hbtqi-historia, Malmö Stadsarkiv
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Nobelvägen
entries.summary: Nobelvägens framdragning.
entries.description: Nobelvägens framdragning. På vänster sida av vägen skymtar gasverkets trumma och på höger sida syns MOHAB (Oljeslageriets) skorsten. Foto: Otto Ohm / Historisk bildbyrå / Malmö Museer

entries.name: Båstadsgården & Barnrikehusen
entries.summary: Båstadsgården, två hus som byggdes som bostadsrätter.
entries.description: Båstadsgården, två hus som byggdes som bostadsrätter. De två husen bakom är kända som Barnrikehusen och byggdes ca 1936. De var moderna hus med ljusa genomgående lägenheter med centralvärme, badrum med toalett, gasspis, sopnedkast, vind, källare och tvättstuga. För att få bo här krävdes minst tre barn i familjen. Här växte författaren Mary Andersson upp med föräldrar och sex syskon i en trerummare på 65 kvadratmeter. Foto Stadsarkivet

entries.name: Ekströms skomakeri
entries.summary: That s a shoemaker standing in his doorway greeting us.
entries.description: That s a shoemaker standing in his doorway greeting us. The door has been built over and the building has been significantly altered since the photograph was taken. Malmö's great Art Nouveau architect Oscar Hägg designed the building, which was completed in 1906. The stucco depicts, among other things, a vigilant owl and a cat playing with a ball of yarn. It was a beautiful facade, but the small apartments behind it were nothing special they lacked amenities and had an outdoor toilet in the backyard. The building originally had 34 one- and two-room apartments. In 1976, the balconies were taken down and most of the decorative facade was removed. Apartments were merged, and 34 became 19. Photograph: Malmö stadsarkiv
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Nya Sofielundsskolan
entries.summary: Sofielund s old primary school sat beside an allotment site, Thulekolonin, which was set up in the 1910s.
entries.description: Sofielund s old primary school sat beside an allotment site, Thulekolonin, which was set up in the 1910s. The city of Malmö acquired the land in 1923, and earmarked it for future expansion of the school. It took a quarter of century for the expansion to take place Nya Sofielundsskolan ( The New Sofielund School ) was completed in 1949. Designed by Sture Fröl n, it s an example of the nyrealism architecture style that was popular in Sweden at the time. On opening, it was Sweden s largest school the dining room could seat 800 students. The bronze statue by the entrance is called The Magnifying Glass , and was made by Gustav Nordahl in 1953. One of the school s most notable former students is the adventurer Renata Chlumska. She was the first Swedish woman to climb Mount Everest. Photograph: Malmö stadsarkiv
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Folkets Hus
entries.summary: In December 1947, the venerable Folkets Hus in Torpgatan (Sweden's first purpose built People s House) was replaced by a more modern structure on Nobeltorget.
entries.description: In December 1947, the venerable Folkets Hus in Torpgatan (Sweden's first purpose built People s House) was replaced by a more modern structure on Nobeltorget. Designed by Hans Westman, it provided a space for political and trade union activities, as well as a theatre. Södra Teatern (the Southern Theatre) was home to a branch of Malmö City Theatre, and it was a popular venue through the 1940s, 50s and 60s. Specialising in comedies and revues, Swedish theatre luminaries like Karl Gerhard, Povel Ramel Maritta Marke and Zarah Leander all performed there. Since 2006, it s been home to Moomsteatern a theatre company noted for its work with actors with learning disabilities. Photograph: Jeanette Rosengrens samling
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: AB Kvarnmaskiner
entries.summary: When it founded in 1867, this company was called Malmö Franska Kvarnstensfabrik Malmö French Millstone Factory even though it was actually Danish-owned.
entries.description: When it founded in 1867, this company was called Malmö Franska Kvarnstensfabrik Malmö French Millstone Factory even though it was actually Danish-owned. The French part of the name came from their use of French quartz, a development that had revolutionized the flour production industry. The millstones they produced were thus often known as fransyskor French girls. This nickname didn t seem to catch on outside of Sweden. They moved from near the harbour to these spacious premises (6400 m 2 ). They continued to trade until 1974, under their later name Kamas Kvarnmaskiner. Photograph: Malmö stadsarkiv
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Folkets Funfair
entries.summary: From the beginning, the management had envisaged Folkets Park as a place with swings and carousels.
entries.description: From the beginning, the management had envisaged Folkets Park as a place with swings and carousels. There were more grown-up attractions in its early years, like test-your-strength games and shooting ranges, but only when the park expanded northwards was there enough space for a bone fide funfair. It arrived in 1926, with a funicular railway, ferris wheels, dodgems, and carousels. In a publication marking the park s 40th anniversary, one of its pioneering administrators, Nils Petter Hansson, said that the only facility in the world that matched Folkets Park was Coney Island in New York. There have been many rides in the park over the years, but in 2014 the management chose to stop renting out areas as amusement parks. Foto: Ur Jeanette Rosengrens samling

entries.name: Kürzels spinnerier
entries.summary: In 1896, Fritz K rzel opened a spinning mill here, named K rzels Fabriker AB.
entries.description: In 1896, Fritz K rzel opened a spinning mill here, named K rzels Fabriker AB. It became one of the largest in the city, producing dresses, rugs, and cloths for cleaning. In the 1940s, they had around 600 employees who benefited from a thoughtful personnel policy. For example, those with young children could bring them to work, where they would be put on to the company bus and driven to a Villa Midhem (close to where the motorway now enters Malmö) whereby they would be taken care of and brought back at the end of the working day. The building is also nicknamed Ugglanhuset (The Owl House), on account of the stone owl, just out of picture. Photography company Kungsfoto would later have their premises here for many years.

entries.name: Malmö Central Prison (1914-2015)
entries.summary: In Sweden, homosexual acts were illegal until 1944.
entries.description: In Sweden, homosexual acts were illegal until 1944. Men were prosecuted for "fornication that is against nature". During the 20th century, there were three major lawsuits in Malmö, in which 34 men were prosecuted. The men were of varying ages, occupations, and social standings. In the last push, in 1940, 20 men were brought to trial. Four were sentenced to hard labour at the now closed Central Prison in Kirseberg. Foto: Malmö Stadsarkiv Text: A Ride to Pride en kartguide till Malmös hbtqi-historia, Malmö Stadsarkiv

entries.name: Malmö Rådhus court
entries.summary: In 1940, around 20 gay men were prosecuted for "moral crimes" at the Rådhus Court.
entries.description: In 1940, around 20 gay men were prosecuted for "moral crimes" at the Rådhus Court. One of them was an aristocrat and former military officer. In a letter, he appealed for a conditional sentence as, "serving a sentence of imprisonment in front of my family would mean complete disaster". The sentence was two months' imprisonment, but the Court of Appeal changed it to a suspended sentence. Six months later, he took his own life. entries.name: Drottningtorget
entries.summary: Drottningtorget är uppkallat efter drottning Fredrika av Baden, gift med den svenske kungen Gustav IV Adolf.
entries.description: Drottningtorget är uppkallat efter drottning Fredrika av Baden, gift med den svenske kungen Gustav IV Adolf. Kungafamiljen bodde i staden i ett halvår 1806 07 och båda makarna biföll nådigt stadens önskan om att få uppkalla två torg efter dem. Vid platsen för torget hade tidigare stadens befästningsverk funnits och ännu tidigare stadens utpost åt öster, österport. Den 15 maj år 1900 öppnades stadens första saluhall i det gamla ridhuset som byggts redan 1819 åt husarregementet. 1965 blev det en privat samling av fordon som öppnade under namnet Vagnmuseum. Numera finns restaurang med fransk anknytning i huset, boulespel idkas och vi får väl anta att den glade vinnaren enligt tradition bjuder på pastis, laget runt. Foto: Jeanette Rosengrens samling

entries.name: Maskinfabriks Aktiebolaget Thule
entries.summary: Formed in 1908, this company specialised in machine tools and, a little later, industrial planers and saws.
entries.description: Formed in 1908, this company specialised in machine tools and, a little later, industrial planers and saws. As they expanded, more room was needed, and in 1942 they built the large machine hall. Six years later, they built offices at the intersection of Lönngatan and Lantmannagatan. By the late 1950s, though, it was all over for Maskinfabriks AB Thule the business folded. Since then a steady flow of businesses have taken up the premises. åkermans used the space to build diggers and construction equipment. It was a vocational school for a while, then Malmö City Theatre moved in at the end of the 1970s and built props there. Since 2008, it s been home to Garaget, a library, cafe, and community meeting-place. Photograph: Malmö-boken, 1946

entries.name: Hollywood 1943
entries.summary: Efter första världskriget rådde akut bostadsbrist i Malmö och staden uppförde ett antal nödbostäder.
entries.description: Efter första världskriget rådde akut bostadsbrist i Malmö och staden uppförde ett antal nödbostäder. Bland annat byggdes dessa hus som uppfördes mellan Sorgenfrifarmen och renhållningsverket i början av 1920-talet. Husen skulle vara tillfälliga men blev kvar i många årtionden. Här bodde fattiga familjer med många barn under trånga omständigheter med enkelglas i fönstren och kallvatten i kranen. Det officiella namnet på träbarackerna var Sorgenfrihusen. I folkmun blev smeknamnen istället Hollywood, Klondyke, Beverly Hills, Pinnatorp, Pinnhusen och Diplomatstaden. Foto Okänd

entries.name: Konsthallstorget
entries.summary: On the left of the photograph, you can see Malmö s craft guild (Malmö Hantverksförening), which was designed in 1916 by the prolific architects Ewe and Melin.
entries.description: On the left of the photograph, you can see Malmö s craft guild (Malmö Hantverksförening), which was designed in 1916 by the prolific architects Ewe and Melin. To the right of the church opposite where Malmö Art Gallery currently stands lies the Johannes colonies (Johanneskolonierna). These were established in 1909 to provide both housing and leisure. Every colony (there were about 60 in total) comprised a small cottage and garden area, bordered with a small fence. The cottages would often have ornamental door and window frames in the snickarglädje style (snickarglädje literally means carpenter s delight ). The greenery you can see behind the fences on the right are likely the result of the hard work of the residents and visitors there. This all came to an end when Pilgården was built in 1943. Pilgården, which housed a restaurant and bowling alley, was inaugurated by prime minister Per Albin Hansson. The building still stands here today. Photograph: Jeanette Rosengren s collection

entries.name: Lars-Eric Tornberg 1921-1943
entries.summary: Lars-Eric Tornberg var en av 33 besättningsmän ombord på u-båten Ulven då den gick på en tysk mina utanför Marstrand i april 1943.
entries.description: Lars-Eric Tornberg var en av 33 besättningsmän ombord på u-båten Ulven då den gick på en tysk mina utanför Marstrand i april 1943. U-båten bärgades i augusti samma år och fördes in till Göteborg för en minneshögtid för de omkomna. Därefter sändes kvarlevorna av de unga männen till respektive hemorter. Ulvens historia har dokumenterats i artiklar, böcker och finns också med i handlingen i Bo Widerbergs sista film Lust och fägring stor där Björn Kjellman spelar en av de som förolyckades.

entries.name: The mountain roller coaster
entries.summary: From Arbetet newspaper, April 1944 The huge roller coaster in Malmö Folkets Park, whose silhouette provided a mountain landscape in Möllevången, no longer exists.
entries.description: From Arbetet newspaper, April 1944 The huge roller coaster in Malmö Folkets Park, whose silhouette provided a mountain landscape in Möllevången, no longer exists. On Saturday morning, it was completely destroyed by a fire that could have had catastrophic consequences under different conditions and without the fast, methodical response of the fire brigade. As it was, the fire was confined to the roller coaster itself. Somewhat surprisingly, the wooden frames of the carousels and miniature car track were saved, even though they sit close to where the fire broke out. There was also a sports hall underneath the roller coaster. After the fire, a bear cave, haunted house, and games arcade were built in their place. entries.summary: Alfred Benzon AB grundades år 1900 och bestod av fem avdelningar: Kemikalieavdelningen - tillverkning av syror och gaser.
entries.description: Alfred Benzon AB grundades år 1900 och bestod av fem avdelningar: Kemikalieavdelningen - tillverkning av syror och gaser. Kolonialvaruavdelningen - tillverkning av bland annat bakpulver, puddingpulver , såskulör (soya), putsmedel och skurpulver. Kolonialavdelningen förpackade även icke-egentillverkade kryddor och essenser. Dessa gick under varunamnet Benzona. Maskinavdelningen - främst tillverkning och försäljning av Benzona Mjölkningsmaskin. Pennavdelningen - tillsyn, reparation och försäljning av pennor. entries.description: Furniture started to be made here in 1893, when master carpenter Anders Hult n opened his business (A Hult n AB). The company moved into a modern factory in 1947, on the corner of Norra Grängesbergsgatan and Kopparbergsgatan. The furniture made here was mostly for commercial use it would sit in department stores, banks, shops and offices, with customers all over the country. For more than twenty years after her husband's death, Emilia Hult n ran the business. Photography: Malmö-boken, 1946

entries.name: Anna 1860-1934 & Eva Bunth 1862-1947
entries.summary: Anna och Eva Bunth var pedagoger som ivrade för flickors utbildning.
entries.description: Anna och Eva Bunth var pedagoger som ivrade för flickors utbildning. 1887 grundade de en privatskola för flickor i Malmö och året därpå blev deras systrar, Clara och Frederique anställda som lärare. Brodern Oscar Albert blev också medarbetare. Skollokalerna byttes över tid. Man flyttade 1905 till den vackra byggnaden på Slottsgatan, ritad av Carl Ferdinand Rasmussen 1878. 88 elever fanns på skolan vid denna tid och kollegiet bestod av 13 lärarinnor och fyra lärare. De båda systrarna undervisade i olika ämnen; Anna i bibelläsning, biblisk historia, katekes, engelska och välskrivning. Eva undervisade i franska. Clara i sin tur hade hand om välskrivning och handarbete och Frederique hade uppsikt över skrivningarna. 1936 beslöt stadsfullmäktige att inrätta en kommunal flickskola i Malmö. De olika privatskolorna ombildades då och uppgick året därpå i Kommunala flickskolan.

entries.name: Kai finds love at Hipp
entries.summary: In the spring of 1949, Hipp aka Malmö Hippodrome welcomed Stockholm s Casino Revue.
entries.description: In the spring of 1949, Hipp aka Malmö Hippodrome welcomed Stockholm s Casino Revue. Their ensemble included Kai Gullmar, one of Sweden's great schlager composers. Gullmar, who according to Sydsvenskan, "trudged in and out of the sketches in her own style", found love here in the form of Danish-born Rita Rosenberg who worked in Hipp's ticket office. Rosenberg had previously performed as a dancer throughout Malmö. The two women began a relationship and Kai's composition First You Come, Then Nothing (Först Kommer Du Sen Ingentin) is dedicated to Rita. Foto 1: Av Photo by Jarl Ekenryd (TT) - Populär Historia, 2019:1, sid 41, Public Domain, https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=78366679 Foto 2: Jeanette Rosengrens samling Text: A Ride to Pride en kartguide till Malmös hbtqi-historia, Malmö Stadsarkiv

entries.name: Per Albin Hansson bust
entries.summary: Emil Näsvall made this bust of Social Democratic politician Per Albin Hansson (1885 1946).
entries.description: Emil Näsvall made this bust of Social Democratic politician Per Albin Hansson (1885 1946). Hansson grew up in a house on the road which now bears his name Per Albin Hanssons Väg. The house has been turned into a museum in his memory. When he was 13 years old, his family moved from Fosie to the Korpen neighbourhood of Malmö. In his 20s, Hansson met his fianc e Sigrid Vestdahl, and moved to her home on Kristianstadsgatan, just a couple of paces from where his bust has stood since 1949. Per Albin Hansson was Prime Minister of Sweden twice, from 1932 to 1936 and from later that year until 1946. Foto 1: Ur Min ungdoms park Foto 2: Ur Svensk Damtidning

entries.name: Björngrottan
entries.summary: It's seems scarcely believable now, but as recently as the 1950s Folkets Park had its own bear cave.
entries.description: It's seems scarcely believable now, but as recently as the 1950s Folkets Park had its own bear cave. It was home to three bears Finn, Fina and Finette. From time to time (especially on warm summer days) a drunk person would fall into the bear pit but, somewhat extraordinarily, there were never any serious mishaps. Leftover cakes and pastries from the Far i Hatten cafe often ended up as bear food. Rather cakes than people, I suppose. Photograph: Bilder i syd, Jeanette Rosengrens samling

entries.name: Anita and Hornet
entries.summary: The corner building here was home to Caf Hörnet (literally, The Corner Cafe).
entries.description: The corner building here was home to Caf Hörnet (literally, The Corner Cafe). When it was modernized in the 1950s, it became known as "Cozy Corner", the hub of the city's jazz life. The dots over the o on the neon sign disappeared at some point, and it became, simply, Hornet ( The Horn'). The building was demolished in the 1970s. One of the employees in its heyday was Anita (n e Tage) Nilsson who is said to be Malmö's first known trans person. Dressed in women's clothing, Anita was subjected to ridicule and harassment and was nicknamed Tage Tosa ( tosa is a Swedish homophobic slur). In the novel 'Q', Malmö author Fredrik Ekelund recounts a memory of how they made fun of "this creature with worn pumps, gray-black tights, a pale brown coat and a scarf on his masculine head. When they shouted: Tage! How s it going? , Anita replied in a determined feminine voice: My name is not Tage, my name is Anita! Ekelund also wrote of his own trans-identity,stating: "My name is not Fredrik, my name is Marisol". Foto 1. Lars Hector Foto 2 & 3. Bilder i syd Text: A Ride to Pride en kartguide till Malmös hbtqi-historia, Malmö Stadsarkiv

entries.name: Ghost train
entries.summary: From Max Lundgren's novel Inga Eliasson, Sales Assistant.
entries.description: From Max Lundgren's novel Inga Eliasson, Sales Assistant. The scene takes place on May 1, 1950 when Gunnar Sträng led the first of May celebrations: If only it had been Erlander! But that boring old man! In Folkets Park, the carousels spun, the chocolate wheels squeaked, the balloon bundles swayed in the wind, fastened to the salesmen's belts. There was screaming and life that surpassed all the markets Inga remembered from her childhood. Ole and Gösta Månsson walked arm-in-arm towards the bar, while the girls stood in line at the ghost train. Inga and Astrid disappeared into the darkness. The carriage swayed and rushed straight ahead towards a giant spider, which opened its arms to them with its long, hairy legs." Foto: Jeanette Rosengrens samling

entries.name: Oscar Winge 1884-1951
entries.summary: Oscar Winge, ursprungligen Svensson, var regissör, skådespelare och teaterchef i Malmö.
entries.description: Oscar Winge, ursprungligen Svensson, var regissör, skådespelare och teaterchef i Malmö. 1922 tog han över Hippodromen, en tidigare cirkusbyggnad, och gjorde om den till teater. Den drev han till 1944 då han överlät teatern till sin exhustru Elsa och blev lyrisk chef på den då nyinvigda Malmö stadsteater. I premiärföreställningen En midsommarnattsdröm spelade han själv rollen som Botten Vävare. I sin ungdom var Winge idrottsman och tävlade på hög nivå i såväl spjut som tresteg.

entries.name: Stora entrén
entries.summary: Folkets Park's main entrance on Amiralsgatan isn t its the oldest that can be found a short distance away on Norra Parkgatan.
entries.description: Folkets Park's main entrance on Amiralsgatan isn t its the oldest that can be found a short distance away on Norra Parkgatan. The park has had several different entrance buildings through the ages. The original was fairly plain and low, but it was replaced in 1952 by a fantastic 650m steel pipe construction, designed by Fritz Jaenecke and Sten Samuelsson. In 1985, the Social Democrats were voted out of power in Malmö for the first time in 66 years, to be replaced by a more conservative majority. A new entrance was built at this time, and the park s name changed from Folkets Park (literally, the people s park) to Malmö Park. The conservatory next to the entrance today was originally built at the Bo01 housing complex, at what is now Västra Hamnen. entries.name: Amiralen (from Amiralsgatan)
entries.summary: From Bo Widerberg's 1952 novel, Hösttermin: Then came Folkets Park, with the vibrant colours of its cramped carousels and Amiralen s exaggeratedly wide arch; mo
entries.description: From Bo Widerberg's 1952 novel, Hösttermin: Then came Folkets Park, with the vibrant colours of its cramped carousels and Amiralen s exaggeratedly wide arch; more than anything, the dancehall looked like an aeroplane hangar. But there the street widened, and became airy under the thick foliage of chestnut trees; you could imagine this is what a Parisian boulevard looked like. He remembered Amiralsgatan in the spring when the chestnuts swelled. When the sun shone on this street after the rain, it was perhaps more beautiful than any other in town. entries.name: Gustav Möller bust
entries.summary: On 24 August 1952, the bust of the former minister of social affairs and trade was unveiled in the presence of the man himself.
entries.description: On 24 August 1952, the bust of the former minister of social affairs and trade was unveiled in the presence of the man himself. Gustav Möller (1884-1970) was born in Malmö, grew up on Tallgatan (now Möllevångsgatan's extension to the west) and worked at the Social Democrat newspaper Arbetet, before becoming head of the book publisher Tiden. As minister of social affairs for four decades, he was involved in several social reforms; public dental care, child allowance, general national pension, and two weeks' holiday all bear his signature. The bust was carved in granite by the Skåne sculptor Ivar Johnsson. Foto: Bilder i syd

De fick tre gemensamma barn. Hilma Tjäder skrev boken Silfversmeden: berättelse om Kina om parets vardagsliv i ett land som dåförtiden fortfarande var tämligen okänt för västeurop er. entries.name: Naima Wifstrand
entries.summary: Naima Wifstrand (1890-1968) was one of Sweden's most famous actresses and operetta singers of the 20th century.
entries.description: Naima Wifstrand (1890-1968) was one of Sweden's most famous actresses and operetta singers of the 20th century. She came from a humble background in a foster family in Stockholm, but found education opportunities in the acting profession. She performed with Malmö Stadsteater late in her career, in the early 1950s, taking several acclaimed roles with Ingmar Bergman as director (she would go on to feature in a number of his films including Wild Strawberries and The Magician). She lived with the female sculptor and illustrator Ninnan Santesson, including a few years together in London. During her time in Malmö, Naima lived at Helmfeltsgatan 10. Under några år på 30-talet var Olga teaterchef för Folkets Hus teater. Hit kom malmöbor i mängd, lockade av folklustspel, humor, sång och kupletter. Malmö Stadsteater invigdes 1944 med Shakespeares En midsommarnattsdröm. Det var man inte sena att utnyttja på Folkets Hus. Där satte man upp En sensommarnattsdröm med Olga i en roll som Thalia.

entries.description: In January 1954, Billie Holiday came to Malmö as the main attraction in a touring mini festival called "Jazz Club USA". The concert was held at Malmö FF s football stadium on Erikslustvägen, but reviews were mixed. Daily newspaper Sydsvenska Dagbladet described her renditions of "Willow Weep for Me" and "Strange Fruit" as exquisite , while jazz magazine Orkesterjournalen picked out My Man along with "Strange Fruit" as the concert s highlights. However, local publications Kvällsposten and Arbetet instead led with, Scandal at the jazz gala. They reported that her voice sounded tired and that she was so inebriated that she could barely stand. She wasn t helped by talking and laughing in the audience, they claimed.

entries.description: In 1953, the MKB housing association built an eight-storey building here, in the Fritz neighbourhood. On the left of the picture you can see Sevedsgatan. Sevedsplan sits behind the high-rise building, on a patch of land that was previously an allotment garden, and a meadow before that. In the 50s, the neighborhood effectively became a small town within the city of Malmö, centred around Sevedsplan. The square housed a bakery, a tailor, a hairdresser, a florist, a tobacconist and a grocery store. When the area was built, cars were beginning to become more common and more thought was being given to traffic management. The city s policy involved building cul-de-sacs, in an attempt to reduce traffic in residential areas and make the streets freer for cyclists and pedestrians.

entries.description: The first thing Sture Lagerwall did when he came to the theatre, was to go into the canteen, pull down his trousers, and lie face down on a table. Nothing happened. Then he got up, buttoned up his trousers, and announced: And this shall be a theatre! In her 2012 book Mitt Malmö Stadsteater from 2012, Kristina Kamnert gleefully tells the story of how her fellow actor Sture Lagerwall introduced himself to new colleagues. As well as being an accomplished actor and film director, Lagerwall was a prot g and lover of legendary stage actor Gösta Ekman Snr. His recollections of his time at Malmö Stadsteater suggest that there were many gay men involved in its early years. Text: Jeanette Rosengren, Kira förlag Foto 1: Postcard from private collection. Hit kom konstnärer som Isaac Gr newald och Ernst Norlind för att utbyta tankar med likasinnade. Thekla och hennes syskon delade också ut stipendier till unga, lovande konstnärer och på 50-talet öppnade hemmet som ett konstgalleri för allmänheten. I nästan 30 år kunde Malmöborna sålunda beskåda målningar, teckningar, grafik och skulpturer i detta privata museum. 1951 fick Thekla Edstrand medaljen Illis quorum. In the photograph, you can see the raised barriers they would be brought down for passing trains and the car traffic would have to patiently wait. On the building, you can see a company name, Oskar Persson. The words down the sides of the door would give Swedish speakers a good idea of their line of business. Kött is the Swedish word for meat, and fläsk is pork. Oscar Persson is mentioned in östen Warnerbring s evocative tribute to the city, When Malmö Smelled (the song title sounds a lot better in the original Swedish När Malmö Doftade). Warnerbring was a celebrated singer, composer, and Eurovision Song Contest winner, born in Malmö in 1935. Here s a translation of some the lyrics: But among all the scents that had something, certainly I ve saved the best for last Oskar Persson came by on his magnificent horse In his butcher shop on wheels Then Malmö smelled, I don t forget, Of sausages and liver pate Then all the people smiled it felt good to be In Malmö, on a completely normal day

entries.description: The legendary boundary-smashing trans person "Merry Lou", aka Marie-Louise Simonsen, ran the Hotell Nornan on Västergatan for a number of years in the 1960s. She also lived there. Marie-Louise was born a biological man, but underwent gender reassignment surgery at an early age. She came to Malmö in the 1960s, where she became well-known for her performances in amateur singing competitions. Her renditions of Zarah Leander songs were especially revered. Alongside Lars Hector she was a popular hostess and entertainer at both Gay House and Trocadero. Text: Jeanette Rosengren, Kira förlag

Förmodligen var det den danske kungens generalbyggmästare Marten Bussert som ritade huset. Antagligen var det tänkt som en sögningegård , en slags övernattningslägenhet för personer som var i kungens tjänst och snabbt behövde kunna nå Köpenhamn. Huset kom snart i det danska handelskompaniets ägo. Kompaniet var en fristad för handelsmän från övriga Danmark som var på tillfälligt besök. Ett stort antal teorier har genom åren framförts angående anledningarna till att planet störtade, både attentat och olycka har varit tänkbara. Pojken i vars födelsenotis det står okänd moder blev så småningom skald, ledamot av Svenska Akademien och chef för Radioteatern. Han växte upp hos fosterföräldrar vid Möllevången. Greta Thott var spritkassörskan som gifte sig in i den skånska adeln när hon äktade greve Stig Thott. Några år efter det att han omkommit i en flygolycka träffade hon Hjalmar Gullberg och blev hans trolovade. Det var på hennes änkesäte, Bökeberg, som Gullberg valde att gå ner i sjön Yddingen, när hans sjukdom oåterkalleligen förvärrades.

entries.name: Thilda Engström
entries.summary: a Here s a description of a typical Malmö woman who lived through the turn of the 20th century: Born Liatorp, Kronoberg County in 1868.
entries.description: a Here s a description of a typical Malmö woman who lived through the turn of the 20th century: Born Liatorp, Kronoberg County in 1868. In her late teens, she moved to Malmö to find a better life. Worked in the textile industry at Manufakturaktiebolaget and Malmö Yllefabriks Aktiebolag, among other factories. Married to manual worker Vilhelm, she would have a total of nine children. Widowed at age 43. Spent her later years living in a one-room apartment in Palmgatan 19. This is a summary of the life of Thilda Engström, who, despite some trying circumstances, lived to the age of 95. The house she lived in stood here, and was demolished in 1964 (the year after her death). The property built on this site went on to house the Swedish Employment Service (Arbetsförmedlingen) for many years. b This is a notice from the Social Democrat affiliated Arbetet newspaper in 1906 that illustrates the impact of poverty in this area. Here s the English translation: From the general public to those who are willing to make sacrifices. A worker by the name of Karl Lindahl, resident in Palmgatan, Sofielund, has been taken into Lund hospital after a long and very difficult illness. He has not been able to recover from his illness and his doctor has prescribed a stay in a sanatorium to regain his health. However, a shortness of sanatorium places means that this isn t possible. The man in question, who isn t a member of a health insurance association and has 3 young children, has had to apply for poverty relief [ fattigvård : the old Swedish equivalent of the poor laws and poorhouses]. His position is especially hard because he fell ill immediately after the long industrial action and strike in the building industry. Therefore, I dare to pray to those who consider themselves as having enough to be able rescue Lindahl, to send me a message. Additionally, it should be noted that the man s lifestyle is impeccable. Jöns Andersson, Storgatan 19, Sofielund c The house on the right was owned for a period in the 1990s by the Hell s Angels motorcycle club. In October 1996, a bomb planted by their rivals, The Bandidos, was detonated. The house was destroyed and a number of windows were smashed in the surrounding area.

entries.description: Hasselgatan was originally called Sturegatan, but together with several other streets nearby, it was renamed when Sofielund was incorporated in 1911. The adjacent Brahegatan became Bokgatan, for example. The photograph shows a small tinsmith s workshop. Since it was taken in 1967, it has been painted yellow, the door has been replaced, and it s generally been freshened up, but its still recognisable. These were drivers of the increasingly influential sobriety movement this was especially prominent in working class areas. Meetings would begin at 8 pm, so that the participants could get home from work and be able to eat their supper before attending. entries.description: Brewing had already been the family business for generations when Malmquists Bryggeriaktiebolag purchased a site and moved their business here in 1898. Fourteen years later, they were one of five Malmö breweries that merged to become AB Malmö Förenade Bryggerier, stepping up beer production from small-scale craftsmanship to large-scale industry. Oak barrels were replaced with enamel casks, and wooden stoppers made way for more modern variants. Drinks company Apotekarnes Vattenfabrik (literally, The Chemists Water Factory) moved here from the city centre, and were given the opportunity to produce Coca Cola under license in 1953. The business unsurprisingly expanded, and built new premises in 1961. Pripps bought the company shortly afterwards. The smell affected the students at Heleneholms school, opposite. entries.name: Ahoy, it’s the Rolling Stones!
entries.summary: The Rolling Stones came to Malmö a few days before their gigs at Baltiska Hallen the summer of 1965, and this photo shows Keith Richards, Mick Jagger and Brian
entries.description: The Rolling Stones came to Malmö a few days before their gigs at Baltiska Hallen the summer of 1965, and this photo shows Keith Richards, Mick Jagger and Brian Jones hitting the boutiques of östergatan. But according to writers Ulf Clar n and Staffan Olander, the fun really started later that day when the band headed out to sea. The concerts had been arranged by Britt Wadner, the indomitable boss of pirate radio station Radio Syd. Her commitment to commercial radio was absolute she was sent to jail on three occasions for refusing to shut down Radio Syd and her powers of persuasion were compelling. The Stones had a gap in their schedule after playing Copenhagen in June, and Britt somehow convinced them to stay in Scandinavia a little longer. The band were ferried out to Cheeta II, the home of the offshore station anchored between Sweden and Denmark. They did a press conference and interview, during which Brian revealed the extent of his shopping spree: We spent an awful lot of money. We went to a lot of shops. I bought about 20 to 30 sweaters, three coats, and about six pairs of shoes . Despite this shopping spree, photos suggest he actually spent most of his time in Malmö wearing a Radio Syd t-shirt. The actual concerts were somewhat underwhelming they only played for about 20 minutes each time and the amplifiers weren t powerful to overcome the noise of the crowd. Nevertheless, the visit was a huge success for Britt and Radio Syd: What a marketing coup! was the headline in the city s Kvällens Post newspaper.

entries.name: The Beatles’ frosty reception
entries.summary: On 14th October 1967, half of The Beatles popped up in Malmö.
entries.description: On 14th October 1967, half of The Beatles popped up in Malmö. Paul McCartney and George Harrison had come to Sweden to meet guru Maharishi Mahesh Yogi at Falsterbohus, a castle in the far south of Sweden. Hunger set in during the Flygbåtarna ferry ride from Copenhagen, so they and their entourage stopped off at Rådhuskällaren for lunch. It was, however, a rather formal establishment with a strict dress code. The Beatles weren t wearing ties so were refused entry. They continued to the Hotel Tunneln around the corner where they were greeted more warmly. In the age of Beatlemania, it was impossible for them to stay unnoticed for long: a passing journalist spotted them, and a crowd of local media soon descended on the hotel restaurant.

entries.name: The Beatles head home
entries.summary: George Harrison and Paul McCartney got a lot of media attention when they visited Maharishi Mahesh Yogi for a weekend in October 1967.
entries.description: George Harrison and Paul McCartney got a lot of media attention when they visited Maharishi Mahesh Yogi for a weekend in October 1967. This photo shows them at the harbor in Malmö, on their way home after staying with the spiritual leader in Falsterbo Castle, south of the city. You can see young journalist Lena Rosendahl talking to George. She d spent the weekend trying to make contact with them and she got her chance at the very last minute, just moments before they stepped on the ferry to Copenhagen Airport. I hadn't thought about what to ask, I was just concentrating on catching up with them, she later told Sydsvenskan newspaper. I managed to ask, what are you doing right now? meaning are you recording an album or something like that. George s reply was typically laconic. "We are trying to get on board a boat, he said before doing precisely that. At the time, it was assumed the Paul and George were visiting the Maharishi for a weekend of meditation, but Peter Brown (the Beatles long-time personal assistant) told a different story in his memoir. He claimed the Maharashi had been negotiating a television series with a US network and promising that the Beatles would appear on the show. Brown thus brought Paul and George to Falsterbo to try and convince the Maharashi to stop using the Beatles for his own PR purposes.

entries.name: Syrener och kalvstek
entries.summary: Malmö entertainer and musician östen Warnerbring had a keen interest in football.
entries.description: Malmö entertainer and musician östen Warnerbring had a keen interest in football. He even played at a decent level, for Sofielunds IF. Here s an excerpt from an article he wrote for the Kvällsposten newspaper: For a couple of years I lived in this community, and I remember the aromas. From the wonderfully sweaty changing rooms in Heleneholm and Sorgenfri, to the smell of empty beer bottles in the dark club rooms on Palmgatan, via that sulphur smell, when "Russin" missed a shot at the pool table. And then the finest scent of all when you came out of the clubhouse on a sunny early summer day and the whole of Sofielund smelled of lilacs and roast veal. Palmgatan 6 had Malmö's last remaining outdoor toilet, which remained in use until 2006.

entries.name: ABBA: the very early days
entries.summary: Malmö played a part in the origin story of global superstars ABBA.
entries.description: Malmö played a part in the origin story of global superstars ABBA. Band members Anni-Frid Lyngstad and Benny Andersson had their first date in March 1969 at Kramer, a notable hotel and restaurant in the city. Anni-Frid had been performing at Kramer with pianist Charlie Norman while Benny was playing with the Hep Stars across town at Arkaden. Later that year Frida took part in Melodifestivalen, the event that decides Sweden s entry to the Eurovision Song Contest. Her entry, Härlig är vår jord ( Our Earth is Beautiful ), finished in fifth place.Malmö played a part in the origin story of global superstars ABBA. entries.name: Judy Garland’s penultimate show
entries.summary: On 22nd March 1969, Judy Garland arrived in Malmö and checked in to the Savoy Hotel.
entries.description: On 22nd March 1969, Judy Garland arrived in Malmö and checked in to the Savoy Hotel. She wasn t in great shape, and it seemed unlikely that she d be physically able to perform her scheduled concert that evening at Kronprinsen's stage. Her gig in Gothenburg a few days earlier had been cancelled. However, local businessman Hugo åberg was determined that the show would go on and offered 90,000 kronor to ensure that the performance would take place. His tactics succeeded and Judy delivered a barnstorming show featuring her most-loved songs including Over the Rainbow . Tragically, it would be her penultimate show, and she died in London three months later from an overdose of sleeping pills. åberg was killed in a traffic accident in Malmö later that year.

entries.name: Jimi Hendrix gets a mixed response at Klubb Bongo
entries.summary: In 1964, Dan Walterström and Per Falck started a pop and rock club called Klubb Bongo.
entries.description: In 1964, Dan Walterström and Per Falck started a pop and rock club called Klubb Bongo. Its first home was the old Folkets Hus on Skolgatan, but by 1966 it had moved on to 18 Friisgatan. With concerts often organised together with the Malmö jazz club New Orleans, it quickly became a popular spot for young people with a passion for music and dancing. Dozens of Swedish and international stars have appeared here, perhaps most notably Jimi Hendrix on 23rd May 1967. It s a gig that s gone down in Malmö folklore. The audience loved it, but the local press hated it. The building was demolished in 1968. Photograph: Bilder i syd

entries.name: N. P. Möller – fastighetsskötare
entries.summary: N. P. Möller, the friendly estate agent, became well-known in the early 1970s as the lead character in the TV programme of the same name.
entries.description: N. P. Möller, the friendly estate agent, became well-known in the early 1970s as the lead character in the TV programme of the same name. He spent his days hanging round Möllevången, with a lively set of accomplices: stray dog Calle, fast-talking corner shop assistant Skogan, and, perhaps most memorably, his neighbour, played by Janne Malmsjö who drank too much and constantly talked about his bygone days on the football field (he went by the nickname Danskdödaren the Dane Killer). Nils Ahlroth, who played the main character, is in the centre of this photograph, with the series' creators Jacques Werup, åke Wihlney, Håkan Ersgård and Frank Andersson. In the series, this street was called Solgatan, but it was filmed right here on Simrishamnsgatan (as well as in many other outdoor locations throughout the city). Photograph: Bilder i Syd

entries.name: Kristianstadsgatan 17
entries.summary: Gunnar "Siljabloo" Nilson (1925-1989) was one of Sweden's greatest jazz performers.
entries.description: Gunnar "Siljabloo" Nilson (1925-1989) was one of Sweden's greatest jazz performers. The nickname came from a hit song the singer and clarinet player wrote in 1953. He was also known for his scat singing. For a period of his life he suffered with a severe alcohol problem, and by the early 1970s he was living ill and forgotten in an apartment here, Kristianstadsgatan 17. He later became sober and made a successful comeback. Siljabloo's life formed the basis of Jacques Werup s 2001 novel "Lev länge dö ung (Live Long Die Young). entries.summary: Ferries left from here to Copenhagen a place that offered richer entertainment and greater anonymity than Malmö.
entries.description: Ferries left from here to Copenhagen a place that offered richer entertainment and greater anonymity than Malmö. It was also in Denmark that the Circle of 1948 and R dstrumperne women's movement were formed. In 1971, the Danes arranged the first women's camp on Fem . Women from around the world participated, and it fostered networks of Nordic activists that would go on to play major roles in the growing lesbian movement. In 1975, the first lesbian week was organized on Fem with 130 participants. Foto: Malmö Stadsarkiv Text adapted from: A Ride to Pride en kartguide till Malmös hbtqi-historia, Malmö Stadsarkiv
